review: 1:1–1:4 — the stanza is Ephesians 1:3–4 (בָּרוּךְ אֵל … אֲשֶׁר בֵּרְכָנוּ בְּכָל־בִּרְכָה … בַּמָּשִׁיחַ … בְּטֶרֶם הִוָּסֵד תֵּבֵל); the Arabic مُبَارَكٌ إِلٰهَنَا … فِيهِ لَقَدِ اخْتَرْتَنَا is that passage, so the Hebrew follows its verbs.
2:4 אֶל־הַשֶּׂה הַהוּא — 'to that Lamb'; the Arabic إِلَى ذَاكَ الْحَمَل points back to the Lamb of 1:4's thought, and Hebrew keeps the demonstrative rather than naming Christ again.
3:1 הִיא הַשֹּׁמֶרֶת אוֹתָנוּ — 'it is what guards us'; the Arabic feminine pronoun refers to grace, and Hebrew keeps the feminine with הִיא.
3:3 בְּחֻלְשָׁתֵנוּ — 'in our weakness', for فِي ضَعْفِنَا; חֻלְשָׁה is the glossary term for weakness and is used again in hymn 76.
4:4 נֹשֵׂא חֶרְפַּת הַצְּלָב — 'bearing the reproach of the cross' (Heb 13:13, חֶרְפָּתוֹ); the Arabic عَارَ الصَّلِيب is that phrase, and חֶרְפָּה is its biblical noun.
